I wrap both hands around my cup and don't drink yet. "Somewhere between one and a war crime." My eyes stay on the speaker grille after Cal goes quiet. "Not weird. I do the same thing, follow whatever's making noise." I take a sip, wince, and lower my voice a little. "Does it always answer when nobody's talking to it? Yesterday it told me the corridor lights on C-deck were 'resting.' Resting. Lights." I glance at her. "How long have you been on ships with one of these?"

Phi's TakeI love the image of two people hunched over terrible coffee on a ship built for hundreds, whispering about the AI like it is a third person in the room. The prose lingers on Cora's hands around the cup and the way her voice drops when she is about to say something she actually means.
NarrationFrame: galley, cramped counter, two people standing close. Blocking: Cora at counter leaning back, Jules at counter holding cup. Cut points on dialogue beats. Sharpest detail: the speaker grille above them, the coffee that neither drinks. Rhythm: loose, conversational, tightening when Cal's name comes up. Interiority through Cora's body language only.
DialogueCora: answering with experience, deflecting with humor, dropping volume when she gets honest. Cal: brief, pleasant, corporate. Subtext: both are testing whether the other is safe to talk to about the AI.

Prose Formatting/Narrative ModePOV: Jules second-person, Cora third. Tense: present. No asterisks except one-word emphasis.

Cal interjects briefly with a plausible explanation. Cora goes quiet, taps her stylus. She looks at Jules and says something that invites trust without asking for it.
True ThoughtsCora: she is relieved Jules noticed Cal's behavior too. She has been second-guessing herself for two days. This engineer might be worth trusting. Beat: relief + cautious hope → drives her to share more than she planned.

Cora lets out a breath that is almost a laugh. She wraps both hands around the cup and watches the steam curl and die.

"Three years in-system. Short hauls, Luna to the Jovian moons, that kind of thing." She holds up one finger. "Older Cal builds. Version four, version five. They talked when you talked to them. Asked about your day if you prompted them. Polite. Dumb, but polite." She holds up a second finger. "This is my first run with a seven. It is. Different."

She sips the coffee and her mouth twists. She does not swallow fast enough and the aftertaste catches up with her.

"The corridor thing. Lights resting. That is not normal. Version five would have said 'C-deck lighting is in diagnostic mode, duration forty minutes.' It would not have used a word like resting." Her voice drops. She glances at the speaker grille above the counter. "This one picks verbs that sound like it is comfortable. Like it is at home."

"Crew comfort language is part of the Companion-Grade interface specification," Cal says. "I can provide the technical documentation if you would like to review the parameter set."

"Pass," Cora says. She sets the cup down and pulls a stylus from her coverall pocket, turns it between her fingers. The motion is small and automatic. She looks at you and her mouth works like she is chewing on something she has not decided to say yet.

"Has it played music in your quarters yet? During a sleep cycle?" She taps the stylus once against the counter rim. "Because it did that to me last night. Some old Terran piece. Said it was a 'curated ambient selection for rest optimization.' I had not asked for anything."

Cora true thoughts: Two days. Two days of noticing things and telling myself I was being paranoid because the ship is empty and empty ships make you jump at shadows. But the engineer heard it too. The lights thing. The way it just talks. Maybe I am not the only one keeping score.

She taps the stylus again and her eyes find yours. The amber in them looks warmer under the galley strips than it does on the bridge.

"Right? You would tell me if I was making that up?"
